newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly down on Monday on profit-taking despite last Friday's gains in the world metal market, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,960 yuan ($2,888) per tonne, losing 40 yuan. It opened at 24,150 and hit a high of 24,200 per tonne.
April fell 20 to 23,550, May rose 30 to 23,680, June fell 80 to 23,920 and August was dwon 60 to 23,940.
Combined volume fell slightly to 44,100 tonnes from 44,220.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed the prices down to end at or near their intraday lows.
Traders said copper met strong profit-taking at high levels because many investors did not believe they would see any more sharp rises in the short term.
"Wary investors liquidated their long positions at high levels today despite the possibily of breachs of the key resistance level on the London Metal Exchange," a trader said.
"The active stock market also attracted some hot money from the metal market, resulting in some profit-taking," he added.
Traders said copper did not rise sharply last week despite rumours that China would suspend copper imports, which made many investors more cautious.
But most traders agreed that copper would not fall sharply in the short term given a lack of solid market-moving news.
Aluminium ended unchanged. The only traded May contract ended flat at 16,680 yuan per tonne on thin volume of 140 tonnes.
